item.title: Trump's Iran strategy: Could this become a forever war?
item.description: The US has launched fresh attacks on military targets in Iran. It wants to prevent Tehran rebuilding its destroyed capabilities, but risks triggering a sustained downward spiral of reconstruction followed by new attacks.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
item.description: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US sanctions halt TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran, disrupting study plans
item.description: Students in Iran can no longer take English-language proficiency exams after the suspension of a US sanctions exemption. Applicants say the move threatens university deadlines and adds costly travel obligations.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can Hichilema heal Zambia's political divide?
item.description: The Zambian president starts a second term after a contested election exposed deep political divisions. His challenge now is to unite the country while addressing concerns over political freedoms.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: South Africa airline behind viral stadium flyby scraps repeat display
item.description: Two passenger jets passed close to Cape Town's DHL Stadium during a flyover last weekend. The carrier said it has shelved plans to repeat the display as South Africa's aviation authority investigates the event.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Malaysia's middle path between China and US faces new tests
item.description: The prime minister's comments on Taiwan and US-backed military facilities near Sabah have revived questions over Malaysia's non-aligned foreign policy.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran bets on shadow networks to evade US sanctions
item.description: To circumvent US sanctions, Iran has spent decades building a complex network of businesspeople and companies. A billionaire once sentenced to death is now back at its center.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Gloria Steinem, feminist activist and journalist, dies at 92
item.description: Steinem became a prominent leader of the second wave of the feminist movement in the US.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US: New York City Mayor Mamdani announces ban on AI for younger students
item.description: New York City is barring elementary and middle school students from using generative AI tools this school year. Meanwhile AI literacy classes and supervised pilot programs will be rolled out for high schoolers.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 1 in 5 youths targeted by online sexual abuse, UNICEF finds
item.description: A survey of around 21,000 young people by the UN's agency for children, UNICEF, has found that online sexual abuse of minors is on the rise.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Is Libya's damaging power struggle about to end?
item.description: The North African country has been divided between two rival governments for more than a decade. Countrywide elections could finally end the split and reunite Libya.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with the UK monarch and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
